newsitem.title: INDIA: Paribas' recommendations on six Indian steel firms.
newsitem.headline: Paribas' recommendations on six Indian steel firms.

text.p: Six leading Indian steel firms have collectively lost 35 percent of their market capitalisation over the last one year, investment firm Paribas Capital Markets said in a report on the Indian steel industry.
"With a combined market capitalisation of $4.5 billion, these companies account for over 80 percent of the India's steel sector's capitalisation," Paribas analyst Rajeev Das said.
The following are major findings of the report:
"- Essar Steel is recovering from CB (convertible bond) redemptions which saw the company repay $72 million for the put option on its 1993 CBs.

This has ended speculation regarding the company's cash flow position. However, plans to raise fresh capital and anouncements of asset sales continue to fuel adverse market sentiment and the company is also facing a tough market for its products. We consider the stock is fairly valued in current market conditions and merits a "no action" recommendation."

"- Jindal Strips faces a put option on its CBs in March 1997 and the market is already focusing on whether the company can honour the put. Its plans of asset sales have been delayed, and a long-denied merger with sister company Jindal Ferro Alloys has not endeared the company to investors.
The stock price has fallen sharply as a result. In view of the problems at the company, we consider the stock is overvalued and merits a sell recommendation."
"- Ispat Industries (formerly Nippon Denro Ispat) already faces scepticism on its ability to honour its obligations in 2001 when its bonds mature, we consider a default is unlikely.

The plan to more than double its plant capacity even before it starts production has alienated investors as has its decision to dilute earnings via a huge issue. We feel the stock is overvalued and merits a sell recommendation."

"- Steel Authority of India (SAIL) has just raised $125 million from international investors. Given its size and marketing muscle, it should be able to withstand the new competition and a focus on reducing costs should make SAIl even more competitive in the future. Whilst we are optimistic on the stock in the long term, we consider it is fairly valued and a "no action" recommendation appropriate."

"- Speciality pipe maker SAW Pipes has suffered a few setbacks lately. It had to cancel its proposed GDR issue, which has altered its expansion plans, and it has lost a potentially lucrative contract. In addition, the company reported earnings below market expectations that had an adverse impact on the stock price.
We consider it is fairly valued and unlikely to outperform the market in the short-term."

"- Tata Iron and Steel Company (TISCO) is also aggressively expanding its capacity. After a record year, it is focusing on funding its new plant which could make it one of the 10 largest steel makers in the world.

On the operational side, it continues to improve efficiencies and cut costs, on the marketing side, it is aggressively expanding into steel service centres in a joint venture with Inland Steel of the U.S. We consider it is fairly valued as it deserves its current premium valuation to sector, and should trade in line with the market."
